subject: Skymap: sudden p99/p95 regressions during deep-context requests
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@skymap.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@skymap.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: large-context requests -> p99 spikes and timeouts

Hi Evelyn —

We started seeing a big jump in p95/p99 latency and a noticeable increase in 500/504 errors around 08:30 PDT this morning. The impacted endpoints are our document-summarization pipeline which routinely sends mixed-context requests (8k, 16k and occasional 32k).

Quick numbers from our side (first 90 minutes):
- p95: up from ~280ms to 1.8s
- p99: up from ~520ms to 8–12s
- Error rate: 0.8% -> 6.1% (timeouts + 500s)

We attached a small perf snapshot and a heapdump. This is affecting our users and we need an ETA for mitigation and a temporary workaround. Can you confirm whether this is tenant-specific or a wider hosting issue?

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Head of Product, Skymap AI

Attachments: perf_snapshot_20271102.json, heapdump_32k_20271102.log

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@skymap.ai>, Skymap Support <support@skymap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: large-context requests -> p99 spikes and timeouts

Alyssa — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I'm escalating immediately.

What I can confirm right now: we saw an uptick in long-context tails across a small number of tenants at ~08:25 PDT correlated with a routing change pushed to a new batching heuristic. We're treating Skymap as priority-1 while we investigate whether the regression is tenant-specific or systemic.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Rolling back the batching heuristic to the previous baseline (ETA: 20m).
- For Skymap only: enabling per-tenant conservative throttling to limit concurrent 16k+ requests to reduce queueing (temporary).
- Karthik/I/O team will collect end-to-end traces and KV-cache hit stats for the affected windows.

I'll follow up with an internal update and a public status note once we have confirmation. Sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts your SLAs.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: [Internal] Skymap P99 regression — traces + mitigation plan

Team — Alyssa reported a high priority customer p99/p95 regression on mixed deep-context traffic (8k/16k/32k). Skymap is a major seat for us (DEAL-8721); Ben, please loop in their AM if needed.

Observed behavior:
- Regression started at ~08:25 PDT, coincident with a small routing/batching heuristic change we promoted to hosted-api cluster group eu/us-fleet-1.
- Symptoms: higher queue depth on certain workers, long tail on KV-cache miss paths, and increased token-generation stalls when guests hit 32k windows.

Ask list (priority order):
1) Karthik — abort and roll back batching change across us-fleet-1 immediately and confirm patch revert (do this first).
2) Markus — gather p95/p99 traces by model variant and worker id; correlate with queue length and async executor latencies. Capture a 30m window starting 08:15.
3) Marissa — enable temporary per-tenant throttles for Skymap to cap concurrent deep-context requests and apply fallback policy to a smaller context model (15k quantized variant) for their tenant only.
4) Ben — notify Skymap AM and coordinate messaging for customer-facing escalation.

We need a 60–90 minute quick turnaround. If rollback doesn't restore baseline, we will apply an emergency capacity bump and disable the new kernel selector for long sequence lengths.

Eve

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Internal] Skymap P99 regression — traces + mitigation plan

Rolled back the batching heuristic on us-fleet-1 at 09:42 PDT (changeset: rb-20271102-batch-v2). Initial metrics look promising — queue depth dropped ~60% on the top-affected workers. I'm still pulling the detailed traces and KV-cache hit/miss aggregates; attaching the snapshot we pulled: perf_snapshot_20271102.json.

If we still see residual tail behavior, we will:
- disable long-seq kernel selector for models with sequence > 16k (hotfix path), and
- enable a temporary serialization gate at the routing layer for 32k requests (limit one concurrent 32k per worker).

Karthik

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Internal] Skymap P99 regression — traces + mitigation plan

Collected traces for 08:15–09:15 window and correlated worker IDs. Findings in brief:
- High variance in executor queueing on workers W-101, W-118; median latencies fine, but long-tail events show serialized kernel backpressure when processing >16k sequences concurrently.
- KV-cache miss rate spiked for the tenant due to a transient prefix variation in requests (lower reuse).
- No obvious OOMs; heapdumps look clean.

Recommendation (actioned):
1) Keep the rollback in place (Karthik) — looks like the primary fix.
2) Apply the temporary per-tenant throttle and redirect Skymap 32k requests to the 15k quantized variant where possible (Marissa, please coordinate with API routing).
3) Open a postmortem ticket to revisit the batching heuristic and kernel-selector interaction (RT-3342).

I'll upload anonymized traces and the worker-level breakdown to the Jira ticket in the next 30m.

- Markus

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@skymap.ai>, Skymap Support <support@skymap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: mitigation in place for Skymap deep-context latency spikes

Hi Alyssa — quick update and next steps.

What we did (completed):
- Rolled back the batching heuristic that correlated with the spike (09:42 PDT).
- Enabled a temporary per-tenant throttle for Skymap on concurrent 16k+/32k requests.
- For 32k windows, we are routing to a conservative 15k quantized model variant as an opt-in fallback; this reduces latency variance while preserving downstream accuracy for most prompts.

What we are still doing (WIP):
- Markus is uploading traces; Karthik is confirming full KV-cache restore metrics.
- We'll monitor p95/p99 closely for the next 48 hours and will alert you if anything resurfaces.

Immediate customer-facing ask: can your team try the opt-in fallback for a subset of heavy users and confirm if the quality meets expectations? We can toggle routing per-tenant and per-route without a deploy.

I've opened a Jira (RT-3342) for the postmortem and longer-term fixes (kernel selector + batching interaction). Ben, please coordinate communication cadence with Skymap.

Apologies again for the disruption. We'll keep this on priority until it's fully resolved.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
